attributes.law_screen: claim.law.address-pre-hoist-survives-every-address-spelling.20260831.v1: SCREENED and its BOUNDARY located rather than violated. The law is right that respelling a single access does not defeat an address-PRE hoist; what defeats it is not spelling the shared address AT ALL. `(u8*)(data + idx + 6)` parses as `((data + idx) + 6)` and therefore literally writes the subexpression `data + idx` into the source, which the neighbouring `data[idx]` access then shares; `(u8*)(data + (idx + 6))` computes `idx + 6` first and never forms it. That is a source-level change of what the common subexpression IS, not a respelling of an address, so the law does not bind. claim.law.dead-nominal-local-area-tracks-declaration-count.20260831.v1: APPLIED as a CONSTRAINT -- slotdiff reports frame T904/O904 EQUAL, so no probe added a declared local. claim.law.int-float-magic-constant-signedness-tell.20260830.v1: screened out for the xoris population by the prior record; not re-derived. claim.law.if-else-arm-swap-controls-fallthrough-placement.20260831.v1: precondition measured FALSE by the prior record; honoured, not re-probed. claim.law.IH_multiset-gain-does-not-imply-fuzzy-gain-arbitrate-with-count-distance.20260901.v1: APPLIED, and this function supplied two of its four measurements.

BASELINE reproduced the prior record exactly and is therefore live: fuzzy 86.9230%, real 1162, insns T1013/O1017, multiset 36t, frame T904/O904. BEST fuzzy 87.1688%, real 1160, insns T1013/O1019, multiset 34t.

THE MECHANISM, read from the aligned view at 0x4a0-0x4e0. Target recomputes each access from the loop index: `addi r0,r31,1 / slwi r0,r0,2 / add r3,r28,r0 / lwz r4,0(r3)` for `data[idx+1]`, then a SEPARATE `addi r0,r31,6 / slwi r5,r0,2 / add r7,r28,r5` for the posPtr. Ours had CSEd `data + idx` into one register and derived both from it: `lwz r3,4(r4)` and `addi r27,r4,24`. The source is what created the shared subexpression, by writing `data + idx + 6`.

WHY ONLY ONE SITE, and this is the reusable warning. Applying the identical regrouping at all four sites closed far MORE of the population -- target-only fell from +4 lwzx +5 slwi +1 add to +2 lwzx +1 slwi +0 add, multiset 36t -> 26t, the largest structural gain of the whole pass -- and LOST fuzzy (86.7710 against 86.9230), because it also grew the function from 1017 to 1023 instructions against a target of 1013. The single site that the aligned view actually implicated grew it only to 1019 and won. A lever verified at one site is not thereby verified at its siblings; see claim.law.IH_multiset-gain-does-not-imply-fuzzy-gain-arbitrate-with-count-distance.20260901.v1.

REMAINING RESIDUAL after the keep: target-only +1 lfs +4 lwzx +3 mr +4 slwi +1 srwi +1 stfs against ours-only -1 lbz -1 lbzx -1 li -7 lwz -1 neg -1 rlwinm -2 stb -3 stw -3 xoris. (a) The SAME indexed-addressing family at the three sibling pointer sites, now known to be individually testable but collectively negative -- the untried step is to regroup them ONE AT A TIME with a fuzzy arbitration each, which is three builds and may yield one or two more single-site wins. (b) The byte round-trip block at 0x4d4-0x568: both sides run the same inlined pbSwap32 lbz/stb chains, but target loads `data[idx-2]` with `lfs` into an FPR and round-trips it through a stack slot before swapping, while we load it with `lwz`. The source form that produces target's `lfs`/`stfs` pair is REVERTED #2 above and it WORKS at the opcode level -- it removed target-only `+1 lfs +1 stfs` outright -- but MWCC then chooses `lfsx` for us where target uses `add`+`lfs`, costing five instructions net; measured 87.1570 with the kept regrouping and 35t/real 1175 without it, so it is negative in BOTH combinations and the pairing was probed jointly per AGENTS discipline 6.
